tagline: League's virtual hip-hop crew woke up Paris with holograms.
headline: True Damage's GIANTS turned the Worlds 2019 final into a hologram concert and made League's champions hip-hop stars.
summary: GIANTS was the debut single of True Damage, the virtual hip-hop group formed by K/DA's Akali and voiced by Becky G, Keke Palmer, SOYEON of (G)I-DLE, DUCKWRTH and Thutmose. It premiered live on November 10, 2019, at the Worlds final opening ceremony in Paris, where the singers performed alongside holograms of their champions, and the music video went up the same day. Seven years later the video has about 234 million views, more than that year's official Worlds anthem, the song has 176 million Spotify plays, and in 2026 True Damage came back to sing the Worlds anthem itself.

story.heading: Akali starts a crew
story.body:
After K/DA's *POP/STARS* topped Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart in 2018, Riot built a second virtual group around the same character. In the new storyline, K/DA's rapper Akali sets out to find new collaborators and forms **True Damage**, a hip-hop collective in which Ekko, Qiyana and Senna bring the vocals and Yasuo handles the production. A teaser began circulating on October 28, 2019, and Riot officially announced the group the next day.

The real voices came from very different scenes. SOYEON of (G)I-DLE returned as Akali, Becky G voiced Qiyana, Keke Palmer voiced Senna, and the rappers Thutmose and DUCKWRTH split Ekko between them. According to Rolling Stone, Toa Dunn, head of Riot's music group, set the vision and picked the artists. The launch was tied to fashion as well: Nicolas Ghesquière, artistic director of Louis Vuitton's women's collections, designed Prestige skins for Qiyana and Senna.

story.heading: Five voices, three languages
story.body:
*GIANTS* was written by the Riot Music Team with songwriter Harlœ, DUCKWRTH and Thutmose; Rolling Stone credited the composition to Kole Hicks and Harlœ. The Riot Music Team produced and mixed it, Benjamin Rice co-produced the vocals, Lydia Paek and Minji Kim handled the Korean translation, and Mike Bozzi mastered it at Bernie Grundman. The track moves from Thutmose's opening verse through Becky G's Spanish *"nada nos puede parar"* and SOYEON's Korean verse, with Keke Palmer carrying the chorus: *we're wide awake now*. Inven Global noted that it was much more hip-hop influenced than *POP/STARS* but shared its wordplay and anthemic chorus.

The cast fit their characters closely. Becky G told Rolling Stone that playing Qiyana felt on-brand because the character is a Latina rapper and singer like her, and that her younger brothers "freaked out" when she asked if they knew League. Keke Palmer said she had to get into the world of Senna, a character cursed as a child, and DUCKWRTH said he picked his jaw up off the ground when Riot asked him to rap as Ekko. SOYEON said she had kept enjoying League after K/DA and was honored to be asked back.

story.heading: Holograms in Paris
story.body:
On November 10, 2019, more than 15,000 fans filled Paris' AccorHotels Arena for the final between G2 Esports and FunPlus Phoenix. ESPN reported that the tickets sold out in seconds. Riot's events team had been planning the opening ceremony since January. Because the indoor arena gave them controlled lighting and they had already done augmented reality, they built what Riot called "holo projection" instead: Holonet, a fabric mesh scrim with metallic filament woven into it, combined with precise arena lighting. Valerie Broussard opened the ceremony with *Awaken*, and Chrissy Costanza and Cailin Russo closed it with the anthem *Phoenix*.

In between, True Damage made their debut. Becky G, Keke Palmer, SOYEON, DUCKWRTH and Thutmose performed *GIANTS* live alongside holograms of their champion alter egos, to choreography by the dance crew the Kinjaz. DUCKWRTH had just come off arena dates with Billie Eilish, and he said performing next to a hologram of himself and his character put League on a level of its own. FunPlus Phoenix then swept G2 3–0. Worlds 2019 peaked at 44 million concurrent viewers, and Riot and Mastercard later released a short film about how the ceremony was made.

story.heading: A neon city with Paris at its heart
story.body:
The music video, made with the animation studio THE LINE, went up on the League of Legends channel the same day the song debuted on stage. It is set in a neon megacity packed with Easter eggs. Qiyana, dressed in Louis Vuitton, appears on an ad screen, Camille's Ferros clan sigil is hidden in the scenery, and subway posters tease projects Riot had not yet released: a young Jinx and Vi for Arcane, a *FIGHT* title card for the fighting game now called 2XKO, and a wanted poster for VALORANT's Jett. When Qiyana sticks out her tongue, it reads *GG EZ*.

Each member gets a different visual world. Qiyana lounges on a throne shaped like the Ixtal crest, Akali raps in the subway, and Yasuo stays at his decks. For DUCKWRTH's verse, the video switches to flat, hand-drawn 2D animation in yellow and purple. The finale was a tribute to the host city: the Eiffel Tower footage was filmed on location in Paris, and the five members appear in front of it one by one for the last chorus.

story.heading: Bigger than the Rift
story.body:
Within a week the video had passed 16 million views. The song had more than 6.4 million Spotify streams and a spot on Spotify's New Music Friday playlist, and Rolling Stone ran a feature on the virtual group "taking over the internet." On Billboard's charts dated November 23, 2019, *GIANTS* reached No. 15 on Rap Digital Song Sales and No. 19 on R&B/Hip-Hop Digital Song Sales, putting a League of Legends skin-line song on hip-hop sales charts.

The numbers kept climbing. By October 2026 the video had about 233.9 million views, roughly 51 million more than the official Worlds 2019 anthem *Phoenix*, and the song had more than 176 million plays on Spotify. YouTube's most-replayed data points to Becky G's Qiyana verse, the part with the *GG EZ* tongue and the "QiQi" line.

story.heading: A producer who never says a word
story.body:
True Damage was built with a twist: Yasuo, the group's producer, has no vocal part at all. Four of the five members get voices, while Yasuo stays behind the decks in every scene.

Riot kept the fandom supplied. The Kinjaz, the dance crew behind the choreography, got their own behind-the-scenes video in December 2019. When Prestige True Damage Senna arrived in February 2020, Riot released a creator kit with an XSplit stream overlay, cosplay reference sheets, concept art and high-resolution wallpapers taken from the music video.

story.heading: The giants wake up again
story.body:
In 2019, Toa Dunn told Rolling Stone he wouldn't be surprised to hear more from the group, adding that anything was possible. Seven years later, on September 29, 2026, Riot announced that True Damage would perform the Worlds 2026 anthem, *Know My Name*, the first time one of its virtual artists had performed a Worlds anthem. SOYEON returned alongside Coco Jones, Vic Mensa and Sofía Reyes. The music video, which premiered on October 8, follows Faker on the road to T1's three-peat, and the group is set to perform at the Worlds 2026 final at Barclays Center in Brooklyn on November 14.

The fiction came back too. The FADER ran an interview with Ekko himself, who recalled people asking him for autographs at the bodega after *GIANTS* came out. The single that introduced a hologram hip-hop crew in Paris had grown into a franchise strong enough to carry the Worlds anthem itself.

whyItMatters: It showed that K/DA was not a one-off: True Damage was Riot's second virtual group, built around the same Akali, and HEARTSTEEL followed in 2023.

Its live debut introduced Riot's "holo projection" (Holonet mesh plus precise lighting) at the Worlds 2019 final in Paris, in front of more than 15,000 fans at a Worlds that peaked at 44 million concurrent viewers.
It brought together Latin pop star Becky G, K-pop rapper SOYEON, actor-singer Keke Palmer and rappers DUCKWRTH and Thutmose in one track sung in English, Spanish and Korean.

It crossed into music culture: it landed on Billboard's Rap (No. 15) and R&B/Hip-Hop (No. 19) Digital Song Sales charts and Spotify's New Music Friday, and Rolling Stone gave it a feature. Louis Vuitton's Nicolas Ghesquière designed Prestige skins for the launch.
It lasted: about 234 million YouTube views (more than the official Worlds 2019 anthem Phoenix) and over 176 million Spotify plays by 2026.
Its success brought True Damage back in 2026 as the first Riot virtual artist to perform a Worlds anthem, Know My Name.

communityMoments.title: True Damage revealed, in Louis Vuitton
communityMoments.description: After a teaser surfaced on October 28, Riot announced the virtual hip-hop collective and its singers, along with Prestige skins for Qiyana and Senna designed by Louis Vuitton's Nicolas Ghesquière.

communityMoments.title: The music video drops the same day
communityMoments.description: Riot premiered the THE LINE-animated music video on the League of Legends channel shortly after the ceremony performance.

communityMoments.title: Rolling Stone and New Music Friday

keyMoments.label: A neon city full of nods
keyMoments.description: The video opens on a neon megacity whose signs and screens are packed with Riot Easter eggs.

keyMoments.label: Easter-egg subway
keyMoments.description: Akali walks past subway posters teasing projects Riot had not yet released: Arcane's young Jinx, a FIGHT card for the game now called 2XKO, and a wanted poster for VALORANT's Jett.

keyMoments.label: Thutmose's verse
keyMoments.description: Thutmose opens the song as Ekko, who flips upside down in a stairwell, on the way to the "I'm a Benz and you're more like a Volvo" line.

keyMoments.label: "Ay, no one can stop us"
keyMoments.description: Becky G's pre-chorus surrounds Qiyana in pink light, then switches to Spanish with "nada nos puede parar".

keyMoments.label: "We're wide awake now"
keyMoments.description: Senna steps out of the mist and Keke Palmer sings the first chorus.

keyMoments.label: Qiyana's verse
keyMoments.description: Becky G's verse begins with Qiyana in a glittering red set, the stretch of the video YouTube marks as most replayed.

keyMoments.label: GG EZ
keyMoments.description: Qiyana sticks out her tongue to reveal "GG EZ" on the "Now they ask where QiQi's at" line.

keyMoments.label: Akali raps in Korean
keyMoments.description: SOYEON's Korean verse plays out in a subway station, with Akali crouched by the escalators and Ekko behind her.

keyMoments.label: Throne, then second chorus
keyMoments.description: Qiyana lounges on her Ixtal-crest throne before the video cuts to Senna for the second chorus.

keyMoments.label: DUCKWRTH's verse goes 2D
keyMoments.description: DUCKWRTH's verse switches the video to flat, hand-drawn 2D animation in yellow and purple.

keyMoments.label: Final chorus
keyMoments.description: Senna returns in shafts of light as the last chorus kicks in.

keyMoments.label: True Damage in Paris
keyMoments.description: The five members appear one by one in front of the Eiffel Tower, filmed on location in Paris.

keyMoments.label: Sleeping giants
keyMoments.description: On the last "sleeping giants", the whole group strikes a final pose in front of red pillars before the True Damage logo.

keyMoments.label: Hologram Ekko
keyMoments.description: A towering hologram of Ekko appears next to a glowing dome as the Worlds 2019 opening ceremony performance begins.

keyMoments.label: Thutmose goes live
keyMoments.description: Thutmose, in a red-and-white varsity jacket, raps the first verse on stage.

keyMoments.label: Becky G in the ring
keyMoments.description: Becky G sings the pre-chorus inside a glowing orange ring on a red set, echoing Qiyana's scenes in the video.

keyMoments.label: Keke Palmer's chorus
keyMoments.description: Keke Palmer sings the first "we're wide awake now" chorus as blue-green smoke graphics swirl behind her.

keyMoments.label: DUCKWRTH's verse
keyMoments.description: DUCKWRTH, in a denim jumpsuit, raps his verse while neon graphics flash across the holo screen, including a "SHEESH!" speech bubble.

keyMoments.label: All together for the finale
keyMoments.description: The singers regroup with the dancers on stage for the final chorus, just before the True Damage logo closes the performance.

featuredClip.description: On "we're bigger than giants", the members appear one by one in front of the glittering Eiffel Tower until all five are lined up, then the video cuts to Qiyana dancing in front of red pillars.
